questions.question: What is the acceleration-time graph of the body when it is at stationary phase or moving in uniform velocity?
questions.questionHtml: What is the acceleration-time graph of the body when it is at stationary phase or moving in uniform velocity?

options.text: Parallel to the time axis on negative acceleration axis
options.html: Parallel to the time axis on negative acceleration axis

options.text: straight line coinciding with time axis.
options.html: straight line coinciding with time axis.

questions.solution: When a body is stationary or moving with uniform velocity, its acceleration is zero. In such cases, the acceleration-time graph is a straight line coinciding with the time axis. This indicates no change in velocity over time.

questions.question: Which one of the following is the unit of length used to measure nuclear distances?
questions.questionHtml: Which one of the following is the unit of length used to measure nuclear distances?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Fermi.

Key Points

  • Fermi is a unit of length used to measure nuclear distances, = 10⁻¹⁵ meters. Hence option 2 is correct.
  • It is named for the Italian physicist Enrico Fermi (1901–1954).
  • A fermi is equivalent to a femtometer and is the older non–SI measurement unit of length.
  • Femtometer is a derived metric measurement unit of length.
  • Since it is a typical length-scale, and often referenced in nuclear physics. 

Additional Information

  • Angstrom is the unit of length used to measure the wavelength of light, 1 Å = 10-10 m.
  • A light-year is the unit of length for measuring astronomical distances.
  • Light year = distance traveled by light in 1 year = 9.4605 × 1015 m.
  • Astronomical unit = Mean distance between the sun and earth = 1.5 × 1011 m.
  • Parsec = 3.26 light years = 3.084×1016 m.
  • The barn is the unit of area for measuring scattering cross-section of collisions. 1 barn = 10-28 m2.
  • Chronometers and metronomes are time-measuring instruments. The quantity having the same unit in all the systems of units is time.

questions.question: If a box of mass 25 kg is pushed 15 m by a force of ‘F’ N and work done in the process is 480 J. Find F:
questions.questionHtml: If a box of mass 25 kg is pushed 15 m by a force of ‘F’ N and work done in the process is 480 J. Find F:
questions.solution: Work = Force × Distance ⇒ 480 = F × 15, F = \(480\over15\) = \(32\ N\)

questions.question: Which of the following law states that, "The force between two objects is directly proportional to the product of their masses?"
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following law states that, "The force between two objects is directly proportional to the product of their masses?"
questions.solution: Law of gravitation: Every object in the universe is drawn to every other object with a force that is inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them and directly proportional to the product of their masses.

questions.questionHtml: A truck falls off a ledge and drops to the ground in 0.8 secs. How high is the ledge from the ground? (g = 10 m/s<sup>2</sup>)
questions.solution:
s = ut + ½ gt2, s = 0 +  ½ × 10 ×  (0.8)2 [Intial velocity will be zero]

s = 3.2 m

questions.question: An electric washing machine of 750 W is used for 4 hours per day. The energy consumed by the machine in one day will be ________.
questions.questionHtml: An electric washing machine of 750 W is used for 4 hours per day. The energy consumed by the machine in one day will be ________.
questions.solution:
CONCEPT:

  • Electric power (P) is the rate at which work is done by the e.m.f. a source in maintaining current in the circuit. 

​\(P = VI = \frac{{{V^2}}}{R} = {I^2}R\)

  • Electric Energy is the total work done by an e.m.f. a source in maintaining current in the circuit for a given time.
  • Its SI unit is the joule (J) or (kWh).
  • That is given by, Electrical energy consumed = Electrical power × time​​

CALCULATION:

Given that,

Rated power of electric washing machine P1 = 750 W

Amount of time spent = 4 hr

Energy consumed (E1) = power × time ⇒ 750 × 4

= 3 kWH.

We know that 1 kWh = 1 unit

Hence, energy consumed by the machine in one day is 3 units.

questions.question: A concave lens has a focal length 15 cm. If the object is placed at 30 cm from the lens, what is the image distance?
questions.questionHtml: A concave lens has a focal length 15 cm. If the object is placed at 30 cm from the lens, what is the image distance?
questions.solution:
The focal length of a concave lens is taken negative.focal length f = -15 cm,Distance of object u = - 30 cm

\({1 \over v} = {{1 \over f }+{1 \over u}}\)

\({1 \over v} = {-{1 \over 15}-{1 \over 30}}\)

\(v=-10cm\), Hence distance of the object from the lens is 10 cm and the negative sign signifies a virtual image.

questions.question: If a current of 1.5 A is maintained in a resistor of 10 Ohm, then the energy dissipated in the resistor in 1 minute will be:
questions.questionHtml: If a current of 1.5 A is maintained in a resistor of 10 Ohm, then the energy dissipated in the resistor in 1 minute will be:
questions.solution:
Use formula: Energy (E) = I² × R × t
E = (1.5)² × 10 × 60 = 2.25 × 10 × 60 = 1350 J

questions.question: Which one of the following is a reason why the weight of a person different on Earth and the moon?
questions.questionHtml: Which one of the following is a reason why the weight of a person different on Earth and the moon?

options.text: Influence of radioactive elements in space on person
options.html: Influence of radioactive elements in space on person

options.text: Absence of atmosphere on the moon
options.html: Absence of atmosphere on the moon

questions.solution:
The correct answer is ​Moon's lower gravitational force.

Key Points

  • Weight refers to the force exerted on a body by gravity while Mass refers to the amount of matter in a substance.
  • The Earth's Moon has considerably less mass than the Earth itself.
  • Not only is the Moon smaller than the Earth, but it is only about 60 per cent as dense as Earth.
    • Thus, the gravitational attraction on the Moon is only one-sixth that of the Earth. Hence option 3 is the correct answer.
  • As the force gravity exerts on a person determines the weight of a person.
  • A person's weight is generally one-sixth of their weight on Earth.
  • One thing to note here is that it is only the value of weight that changes from Earth to the moon, while the mass remains the same.
